chunks: The idolaters say: "If God had willed, we would not have worshipped anything apart from Him, nor would our fathers have done, nor would we have forbidden anything without His (leave)." So had the people done before them. Therefore it is binding on the prophets to convey the message in clearest terms.
ai.seo_question: What is the argument of the idolaters regarding divine will in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the polytheists' claim of divine determinism to excuse their deviation, a concept linked to the Jabriyyah school, while affirming the prophets' role as clear conveyors (mubalighun) rather than coercors. It underscores the principle that prophetic duty is limited to clear communication, leaving judgment to God, a theme central to Shia discussions on free will and prophetic infallibility. The verse also connects the current generation's idolatry to that of their predecessors, emphasizing the continuity of human deviation despite clear guidance.
